content.summary: Heart transplantation is the gold standard for treatment of advanced heart failure in absence of contraindications. Post‑transplant 1‑year survival is ~90% with a median survival of ~12.5 years. Transplantation improves quality of life and functional status, but return to work rates may be lower than expected.
main_challenges_after_transplant: Efficacy or side effects of immunosuppression (rejection, infection)
content.donor_recipient_notes: Organ donor shortage remains main limitation. Donor heart criteria have been extended to allow increased upper donor age in some regions. Careful recipient selection based on pre- and post-transplant life expectancy and comorbidities is required.

table17.title: Heart transplantation: indications and contraindications
indications: No other therapeutic option, except for LVAD as bridge to transplant (BTT)
contraindications: Severe peripheral arterial or cerebrovascular disease
Pharmacologic irreversible pulmonary hypertension (LVAD should be considered to reverse elevated pulmonary vascular resistance with subsequent re-evaluation to establish candidacy)
Malignancy with poor prognosis (require oncology collaboration to stratify tumour progression/recurrence risk with immunosuppression)
Irreversible liver dysfunction (cirrhosis) or irreversible renal dysfunction (e.g., creatinine clearance <30 mL/min/1.73 m^2). Combined heart-liver or heart-kidney transplant may be considered
Other serious comorbidity with poor prognosis
Pre-transplant BMI >35 kg/m^2 (weight loss recommended to achieve BMI <35 kg/m^2)
